Source limitations
The source Nq reads unit weight instead of friction angle. Its line-load expressions use qL2 and are not
dimensionally valid kN/m reactions. These outputs are not transferred into the design load path.
Effective slab depth uses a fixed 40 mm deduction. Strength reduction is applied twice in As. The deflection
expression uses effective depth in place of section inertia. Strip soil subtraction and bearing labels mix units.
Bar/mesh lookup alone does not verify minimum reinforcement, shear, settlement or anchorage.

Scope limitations
Uncracked linear elastic trial only; calculated fibre stresses are not a cracking or concrete strength acceptance.
Prestress force is the uniform longitudinal resultant in the linear small-slope model. Tendon stress is nominal force/area, not a verified jacking or cable-path stress.
One prismatic, axially free, simply supported span under uniform loading; identical section and supports at transfer and service.
Stage forces are supplied uniform forces after applicable losses. Their derivation, tendon strength and stressing sequence are not verified.
Friction endpoint calculation is separate and is not a substitute for elastic shortening, anchorage seating, creep, shrinkage, relaxation or a spatial force analysis.
External reactions include actual material selfweight once. Primary prestress is self-equilibrating in this determinate model; no secondary prestress reactions are calculated.
The optional final bonded midspan flexure check is reported separately. No shear, punching, transfer-strength, anchorage, bursting, development, cover or fire resistance acceptance.
No cracked stiffness, long-term or incremental deflection, shrinkage curvature, creep, vibration or prestressed crack-control qualification.
No composite topping, interface, lifting, transport, storage, changed supports, continuity, openings, concentrated loading, bearing, diaphragm or product approval.
Calculation basis
Equilibrium and Euler-Bernoulli curvature of a prismatic uncracked strip. All equations and numerical substitutions are generated from the current Python calculation. No worksheet response, saved JavaScript result, assumed strand layout or product-capacity
table is used.
AS 3600:2018 with the supplied A1/A2 annotated source: clause 2.5.2.2 (transfer action combinations); clause 8.5.3 (short-term and separate time-dependent deformation); clause 9.1.1 (slab flexure reference); clauses 13.3 and 17.3 (transmission/development,
anchorage, installation and bonding). These references identify outstanding qualification categories; this report does not implement their complete resistance or acceptance checks.
Source record: AS3600-A2_annotated.pdf supplied in the user engineering-manual library. The source edition is stated explicitly; no claim is made that this document establishes every current amendment or project requirement.
For hollowcore and other supplied precast sections, manufacturer-verified properties, shear/flexural resistance, strand arrangement, bearing, openings, connections, lifting/storage and erection details are still required. Hollow Core Concrete design guide:
https://www.hollowcore.com.au/pdf_files/Hollowcore_Guide_v7_Book.pdf . No catalogue geometry or resistance is inferred from that reference.
Engineering conclusion
The stage stresses and deformations remain ELASTIC RESPONSE ONLY. Final bonded flexure and minimum nominal strength, when calculated, are limited to the declared midspan section and supplied data. Long-term performance, shear, anchorage, other
sections/stages and complete project design remain NOT QUALIFIED. NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION.
